:::

Ulrike Tillmann is the Director of the Isaac Newton Institute and a Professor of Mathematics at the University of Oxford, where she is a Fellow of Merton College and co-director of the Centre for Topological Data Analysis.

Ulrike has worked broadly in topology, K-theory, and non-commutative geometry. 
Her work on the moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces and manifolds of higher dimensions has been inspired by problems in quantum physics and string theory. 
Some of her most recent work has been motivated by new and developing challenges in data science.

She was awarded the Whitehead Prize by the London Mathematical Society in 2004 and the Bessel Preis by the Humboldt Society in 2008. 
Elected a fellow of the Royal Society in 2008, she was an inaugural fellow of the American Mathematical Society in 2012, and became a member of the German National Academy of Sciences, Leopoldina in 2017. 
In 2025 she received an honorary doctorate from the University of Copenhagen.

She serves on scientific boards of several international institutions, including the Fields Institute in Toronto and the German Universities Excellence Initiative. 
At the end of 2020 she finished her term as a member of Council of the Royal Society where she also served as interim Vice President in 2018. 
She served as president of the London Mathematical Society 2021-23 and is a Vice-President of the International Mathematical Union since 2023.
